title: Roman Theatre of Cartagena
geometryBasis: Mapped retaining arc, inner and outer cavea walks, axial stair and municipal archaeological measurements provide the theatre geometry. The stage deck, irregular seating and remaining columns follow the five cleared exterior images.
sectionBasis: The 1996 excavation report gives 16 lower rows with 0.8 m treads and 0.4 m rises. The municipal museum gives a 43.60 m stage span. Upper surviving seat elevations and foundation contacts are photographic estimates in the unchanged source field.
limitations: This is the exposed 2017 site. The partly restored stage wall and seating are represented as surviving fabric, with adjacent cathedral and museum outside scope.
The lower seating follows published dimensions. The spacing and surviving heights of the upper terraces, stage ruins and column fragments are visual estimates.
The original relief remains unchanged. Exact excavation and exposed floor heights are unavailable, so the visible archaeology and local embedment are approximate.
